name: Battle of Actium
intro: The sea off Actium in western Greece, at the mouth of the Ambracian Gulf. You are Marcus Agrippa, admiral of Octavian, with a fleet of lighter, faster ships and well-fed crews. Mark Antony and Cleopatra have a fleet of heavier ships, some of them giants with towers and bronze rams, but many short of men. Accounts of each fleet range from about 250 to 500 ships.
debrief: In reality, Agrippa took ports on Antony’s supply route, including Methone, and blockaded the gulf; Antony’s camp suffered disease and desertion, and he could not man all his ships. On 2 September Antony’s fleet came out. Octavian’s ships stayed out of range until Antony had to attack, and the fighting went on all afternoon without a decision. Cleopatra’s squadron then raised sail and broke out to the open sea, and Antony followed in a smaller ship; many ships burned from firebrands by nightfall. One modern view holds that the escape was Antony’s plan all along. Antony lost over 5,000 men and many ships taken or sunk; within days his army went over to Octavian. Charging the giants and chasing Cleopatra are what-ifs.

win: Cleopatra’s sails vanish to the south.

options.text: Supplies cut, disease in his camp

decisions.title: The blockade
decisions.text: Antony and Cleopatra have gathered their fleet and army in the Ambracian Gulf. You are Agrippa, Octavian’s admiral. Your fleet is smaller in ships but faster and better crewed.

hint.text: Antony’s supplies come by sea from Egypt and the East.

scout.text: Take the ports on his supply route and hold the sea outside the gulf, and his army will starve and sicken while yours waits.

choices.label: Seize his supply ports and blockade the gulf

fx.text: You storm Methone and other ports on Antony’s supply route and close the sea. Malaria and desertion spread through his crowded camp.

choices.label: Attack his fleet inside the gulf while it is crowded

fx.text: Your ships force the narrow strait and are rammed by the heavy ships waiting inside.

choices.label: Wait at sea for him to come out

fx.text: He waits too, and his supplies still get through.

decisions.title: Antony comes out
decisions.text: On 2 September Antony’s fleet rows out of the strait and forms a line. His ships are huge, with bronze-armoured rams and towers full of archers and catapults.

hint.text: His big ships are hard to board and hard to ram, but they are slow.

scout.text: Close in and his towers will shatter your light ships. Hold off out of range, and he must come to you or sit in the swell.

choices.label: Hold out of range and make him come

fx.text: Your fleet hangs back beyond his missile range. By noon Antony has to move first.

choices.label: Charge at once and ram before his archers find the range

fx.text: Your Liburnians bounce off bronze-armoured bows and are smashed by stones from the towers.
Antony does not take the bait.

decisions.title: Stretching the line
decisions.text: Antony attacks your northern wing with his biggest ships. You are on that wing.

hint.text: As Antony’s wing follows yours north, a gap is opening in his centre.

scout.text: Extend your wing north, making him stretch to follow. His line thins and his centre opens.

choices.label: Extend your wing north, stretching his line

fx.text: Your wing slides north and Antony’s heavy ships follow. His centre thins, and a gap opens.

choices.label: Fight his big ships head-on, where your crews are best

fx.text: The great ships crush your squadron.

choices.label: Fall back toward the rest of the fleet

fx.text: Your line closes up but he keeps his shape.

decisions.title: Swarming the giants
decisions.text: All afternoon the fleets fight. Antony’s big ships cannot catch yours, and yours cannot sink his.

hint.text: Your crews are fresh and your ships fast.

scout.text: Gang up: three or four light ships on each giant, grapple it with the harpax, hurl fire, and board it from every side.

choices.label: Swarm each big ship and throw fire

fx.text: Your ships swarm the half-manned giants, grapple them and fling firebrands. One by one they begin to burn.
You set some of his ships alight.

choices.label: Keep shooting from range; never let them grapple

fx.text: His ships are battered but still afloat.

decisions.title: Cleopatra’s sails
decisions.text: Suddenly Cleopatra’s squadron, in Antony’s rear, raises its sails and drives through the gap in his centre for the open sea. Antony follows her in a small ship.

hint.text: The wind has turned. Her ships are fast under sail.

scout.text: Let her go. The fleet left behind, leaderless and burning, is the prize. Its army ashore will follow.

choices.label: Let her go and close on the ships left behind

fx.text: You let the sails go and close on the rest. By nightfall Antony’s fleet is burning or surrendering, and within days his army goes over to Octavian.
Much of Antony’s fleet is taken.

choices.label: Chase Cleopatra with your fastest ships and take the treasure

fx.text: The chase scatters your fleet, and part of Antony’s gets away.

choices.label: Send half the fleet after her

fx.text: Neither half does its job well.
